recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reintroducing a Consent.scope edit would conflict with the later FHIR-31903 model change; future consent-scope terminology changes should go through terminology/THO or a new Consent.category-focused tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-17559 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked to make the then-current Consent.scope CodeableConcept binding extensible because a required four-code scope list prevented non-patient uses, and to rename consent-scope code privacy to patient-privacy.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-17559 was found. Historical commit f4bb6c3d6e changed the consent-scope code and examples from privacy to patient-privacy, and R4 published history shows Consent.scope with an extensible binding to ValueSet/consent-scope and patient-privacy in the consent-scope CodeSystem.
additional_context: Later Published Consent issues changed the model. FHIR-27776 clarified Consent.scope wording for R5, and FHIR-31903 then eliminated Consent.scope and changed Consent.category to 0..* with an example binding to a category value set that includes the consent-scope code system. Zulip discussion for FHIR-31903 supports the rationale that scope and category were duplicative and that category should be the flexible categorization surface.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build has Consent active, no Consent.scope element in source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml, Consent.category as 0..* with example binding, source/consent/valueset-consent-category-example.xml including http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/consentscope, and fhir.ini mapping old Consent.scope to Consent.category.
